title: Warmup stickiness weekly notes
content:
Week: 2027-03-01 -> 2027-03-05
Owners: Aisha (notes), Daniel (experiments lead), Laura (telemetry), Ravi (kernel), Michael (oncall)
Attendees: core runtime, kernel, telemetry, oncall rotation

Summary / goal
- Triage and reduce the recurring tail spikes we observed during midday traffic ramps. Hypothesis this sprint: a subset of KV cache entries are "sticky warmups" — they are treated as warm (cache hits) by some components but are missing useful prefetched state (tile/kv fragments) causing upstream kernels to re-request and serialize batches, producing p95 spikes.
- Run controlled experiments to validate eviction thresholds, prefetch eager vs lazy, and a small kernel handshake change to avoid synchronous rehydrate on miss.

What we observed last week (recap)
- Multiple p95 spikes during 11:45-13:30 PST across dedicated clusters after a short surge of requests from hosted customers.
- Telemetry (Laura): spike correlates with a short-lived cohort of long sequences (~>120 tokens) where the KV cache shows >60% logical hits but kernel-level misses for some tiles.
- Load profile: bursts were ~30s–90s; batching depth shrank because many requests serialized waiting on kernel rehydrate paths.

Experiments run this week (Daniel/Ravi)
1) Eviction bump: raised soft-evict threshold from 0.65 -> 0.78 for the bursty cohort (config A). Result: reduced rehydrates by ~24%, p95 improved from 340ms -> 260ms on the test pool, but average latency moved up slightly (+6ms) for long-running sessions. (JIRA-RT-9876-a)
2) Lazy prefetch toggle: enabled conservative prefetching (only forward +2 tokens) for sequences identified as bursty. Result: increased miss ratio on small tiles but decreased kernel contention. p95 improvement ~12% in the first 60s of a burst. (PR #4218)
3) Kernel handshake change: made kernel return a light "stale-ok" token for secondaries to proceed while async rehydrate continues. Result: throughput improved under contention; observed a small increase in error retries (+0.2%) but application-layer retry mask handled most cases.

Telemetry notes (Laura)
- Added a new KV tag: kv_warmup_state (values: cold/partial/warm/stale). Instrumentation pushed to canary fleet on 2027-03-03.
- New dashboards: warmup-cohort-p95, warmup-rehydrate-rate, kernel-serialize-count. Early canary shows warmup-cohort-p95 dropped 18%.
- Need to correlate these metrics with per-route batching depth and per-client token distribution (next action).

Open issues and hypotheses
- Sticky warmups appear when KV index points to entries that are present but missing tiled fragments used by newer kernels (version skew / incremental kernel rollout?). Hypothesis: rollout mixing (old prefill logic vs new aggregator) causes partial fills.
- Another possibility: eviction races during rapid short bursts leave fragmented entries; the kernel's rehydrate path is synchronous, causing batch serialization.
- Unresolved: why some tenants see no effect — is it correlated with model architecture (decoder-only vs encoder-decoder) or request windowing?

Action items (owners + due)
- Daniel: run A/B across 4 clusters with eviction bump vs default for 72h, collect per-tenant warmup metrics (due 2027-03-08) — JIRA-RT-9876-a.
- Ravi: submit follow-up PR to make kernel handshake opt-in via config flag and include lightweight stale-ok path (PR target 2027-03-06).
- Laura: add per-route correlation in dashboards and hook into alert that fires when rehydrate-rate > 5% for 15m (due 2027-03-09).
- Michael: prepare oncall runbook snippet for midday bursts, include steps to toggle conservative prefetch and eviction bump (due 2027-03-04).
- Aisha: draft a short postmortem-like doc if we fail to see sustained improvement after A/B ends (due 2027-03-12).

Notes to self / rough ideas (informal)
- Could we try a small token-count based admission where requests that would cause serialization are routed to a sibling pool with slightly higher cost but less contention? (routing policy experiment)
- Consider a micro-batch breakpoint: if a request would wait >X ms for rehydrate, proceed with a fast fallback (shorter context) and background rehydrate — trade quality vs latency.
- Explore stronger tenant-aware eviction: sticky tenants keep state longer for the first 3 minutes after a long sequence burst.

Meeting decisions
- Approved kernel handshake flagging as opt-in for rollout.
- Agreed to prioritize telemetry correlation before applying global eviction changes.

Quick numbers snapshot (canary pool vs baseline)
- baseline p95 (midday): 340ms -> canary combined changes -> 270ms (approx -20%)
- rehydrate-rate baseline: 6.4% -> canary: 4.1%
- batching depth median: 8 -> 9 (small improvement)
- tail retries: +0.2% (investigate RCA)

Links and references
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serve-runtime/pull/4218 (lazy prefetch, initial canary)
- Kernel handshake sketch: CONFLUENCE-1234-warmup-behavior-notes
- Triage thread: slack://channel/serving-runtime#thread-xyz
- Experiment dashboard: internal-dashboard/redwood/warmup-canary-2027-03

Next sync
- Quick check-in Tue 2027-03-09 11:00 PST (15m) to review A/B initial data.
- Full review meeting Fri 2027-03-12 14:00 PST (30m) to decide on rollout or rollback.

TODO (short)
- add example traces to confluence (Aisha)
- wire up per-tenant alerting (Laura)
- finish kernel opt-in flag (Ravi)

Random notes / friction logged during run
- Local repro is tricky — need a synthetic client that reproduces short 30s bursts with long sequences. Daniel to share CL.
- Oncall toggles currently require a patch deploy to change eviction threshold; need playbook to make it a runtime config.

—— end of notes
